$comment: Convergence-Impact Gate registry (BI-B19BE117). A changed file matching one of these surfaces reaches an EXISTING install only through some convergence mechanism (self-upgrade promoter, installer re-run, session-start hook convergence, seed re-run) or not at all. The gate does not know which; it requires the PR to say. Keep this registry NARROW: every kind here has a documented instance of biting an existing install. Add a kind only with the BI that proves the bite. Regexes match repo-relative POSIX paths.

surfaces.why: Compose files, Dockerfiles and container entrypoints define the running topology. promote.sh composes from the new release assets, but a dropped service is never removed (BI-922EBB99) and a new volume var is never provisioned (#3262).

A key added to .env.example exists only on installs created after it. The installer writes .env once; an existing install keeps the file it has (BI-FEE77B68 had to special-case DPF_HOST_BIND_ADDRESS).

Installer, launcher, promoter and install-state code is what an existing install runs to become the next version. A change here that assumes the new launcher is already present deadlocks the crossing (BI-BE8BBDE9).
Hook logic converges only when something re-runs the converger. BI-3727106F: 68 of 85 worktrees pushed ungated because convergence was install-time only.
config/ is COPYd into the image and read at boot; a new key or budget changes behaviour on every install that upgrades, and a removed one strands installs that still carry it.

imageCopy.$comment: Files the portal image COPYs BY NAME are parsed live from these Dockerfiles. A rename or move breaks the image build for every install that upgrades. Directory COPY sources are not classified (they are app source, reached by the normal image rebuild); only single-file sources outside the ignore set are.

seedContent.$comment: Canonical seed content is classified through the same registry the Seed-Fit gate uses, so the two never disagree about what is seed. Seed-Fit asks whether the content belongs; this gate asks whether an existing install ever receives it.
